subject: P0 — Skyline Retail: us-west-2 latency & error storm / cross-region shift request
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@skylineretail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - Skyline <contracts@skylineretail.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T08:15:00Z
Subject: Immediate: production errors + latency in us-west-2 impacting checkout

Markus —

We're seeing a sustained spike of 5xxs and elevated latency across our checkout flows that started ~07:50 PDT. Error rate for API v1/checkout is ~15% (was <0.5% baseline) and p95 latency has climbed to ~650ms. Throughput is throttling intermittently (we're observing head-of-line backpressure from request amplification).

Impact: customers seeing failed payments and timeouts. Our engineering dashboard shows a clear correlation with requests routed to us-west-2 (usw2-gpu-pool). We've attached sample request IDs and a packet capture + traces.

Please escalate — our SRE team is on a call and asked whether Redwood can shift traffic away from us-west-2 and enable cross-region fallback. We need a rapid mitigation plan and an ETA for a durable fix.

Attaching: skyline_error-traces.zip, request_ids_sample.txt

Carlos
Sr. SRE, Skyline Retail
ops@skylineretail.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@skylineretail.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: production errors + latency in us-west-2 impacting checkout

Carlos — thanks for the traces, and sorry for the hit you're seeing. We're treating this as a P0. Initial read: an AZ-local kernel regression on the GPU serving fleet combined with a KV-cache pressure pattern has amplified tail latency for models used in the checkout path.

Short plan while we investigate root cause:
- Option A (fast): shift 40-60% of Skyline's checkout traffic to us-east-1 (regional steer) for the next 60–120 minutes. This is a soft-redirect at the routing layer — no model change.
- Option B (if capacity constrained): spin up a warmdedicated pool in us-east-1 + enable a quantized compatible variant for latency-sensitive routes (small perf delta, lower vram).

I am opening an internal bridge now (Sean/Hannah please join). Carlos — can you confirm whether Skyline can accept the partial geo-steer immediately? If yes, share any IP allowlist constraints and whether you want session affinity maintained.

I will follow up in 5–10 minutes with a proposed routing action and the exec ask if the shift requires a cross-region commit/credits.

—Markus
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-30T08:26:00Z
Subject: URGENT: Skyline P0 — us-west-2 throughput & failover plan (proposed)

Team —

Summary: Skyline Retail reporting 15% 5xx on checkout path correlated to request amplification and KVCACHE pressure in usw2. Customer requests immediate cross-region reroute.

Proposed action (execute within next 15 minutes):
1) Apply regional steer: route 50% of checkout traffic from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 via policy (gradual 10% step every 2 minutes)
2) Enable prefix/KV cache warming for Skyline in us-east-1 to avoid cold K/V misses (prepopulate from snapshot)
3) If we see capacity pressure in us-east-1, enable quantized model variant as fallback for the checkout route (tracked by Canary)
4) Open a DocuSign amendment to allow short-term cross-region burst (ops/finance/legal flagged) — I attached a draft (docusign-fallback-amendment.pdf)

Risks & mitigations:
- Increased token egress/costs during reroute (Finance — Monica, please advise likely one-time credit ask)
- Session affinity: opt-in to preserve sticky sessions; otherwise stateless requests will land safely in new region
- Customer communication: Markus will send exec summary and next steps to Skyline (copy to Legal)

Attachments: redwood_routing-plan.pdf (routing steps), skyline_error-traces.zip (from customer).

Please reply with: APPROVE / HOLD / QUESTIONS. If no objection within 5 minutes, proceed with step 1.

—Markus

Date: 2026-09-30T09:05:00Z
Subject: CEO/Exec summary: Skyline P0 (us-west-2) — routing shift in progress + recommendation

Evelyn — quick exec note for visibility and approval on a credit ask.

What happened: an AZ-level serving regression paired with K/V cache churn in us-west-2 caused a surge of 5xx and high p95 on Skyline's checkout route (~15% error rate).

What we've done:
- Initiated gradual regional steer: 50% of checkout traffic from usw2 -> use1 (10% steps every 2 minutes); bridge open and runtime team monitoring
- Pre-warmed KV cache in use1 and enabled compatible quantized fallback; immediate customer-facing errors reduced by ~70% in early checks (p95 dropped to ~220ms for steered traffic).

Recommendation / Exec ask:
- Approve a one-time operational credit for Skyline equivalent to 10% of last month’s usage for the P0 mitigation window while we complete root-cause and restore normal serving in usw2. Monica — please model the estimated credit and authorized range.
- Approve short-term DocuSign amendment to authorize cross-region burst for two hours (attached draft)

Customer impact and risk: high; Skyline is a strategic mid-market account with expansion on the horizon (DL-7821). We should prioritize quick stabilization and keep legal in the loop for the amendment.

I'll provide a full post-incident write-up when we have root cause.

—Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
